## Overview

The available-case modified ITT generalisation contrasts [LRPITT15](../lrp-rli-itt-015) (expressive: TE vs UE) and [LRPITT15b](../lrp-rli-itt-115) (receptive: TR vs UR) each compare taught versus not-taught *within* a modality. Neither asks whether the assigned-arm difference for directly-taught words is larger in the **expressive** modality than in the **receptive** modality. LRPITT16 supplies that missing contrast: the two Block 1 *taught* outcomes — expressive taught target words $TE$ and receptive taught target words $TR$ — are fitted together as factorised marginals over the randomised window, and the headline quantity is the difference between their probability-scale average marginal effects, $\mathrm{AME}_{TE} - \mathrm{AME}_{TR}$.

A positive contrast means the model estimates a larger assigned-arm difference in expected proportion correct for taught expressive words than for taught receptive words. This is a modality contrast, not a taught-versus-untaught generalisation contrast. The conditional logit-coefficient difference is retained as a secondary summary.

Randomisation created exchangeability in the original full randomised cohort, so these offer contrasts require no baseline-covariate adjustment there. The fitted factorised contrast instead conditions on archive inclusion and the required observed variables for both outcomes. A causal reading of either component or their difference requires that this selection did not induce an association between assigned arm and the potential values of either outcome; extending the result to all 57 randomised children requires further missing-data assumptions and sensitivity.

## Design

Two outcome-specific Beta-Binomial marginals are fitted in one graph over the randomised phase-0 window ($G = 1$ intervention, $G = 0$ wait-list), with own baseline and linear age but no cross-baselines. The LKJ residual-correlation block is **off**, so the model does not estimate within-child posterior covariance and the contrast uncertainty is not guaranteed to be conservative. The report uses a common proportion-correct risk-difference scale but treats the result as an exploratory factorised sensitivity, not calibrated paired inference; confirmation requires a dependence-model analysis — the registered companion [`lrp-rli-itt-216`](../lrp-rli-itt-216) (#551), the same contrast with the LKJ residual-correlation block on, published as a posterior difference that carries the estimated within-child covariance — or a paired child-level randomisation-inference/permutation, bootstrap or sandwich analysis. Read the companion's interval and P(> 0) beside this one; the point estimate should agree. PSIS-LOO leaves out a child, not a child-outcome cell.
